A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work despite the changed title. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices are readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original attack experiments on HarmBench across four victim models, including sampling-efficiency results, entropy-objective comparisons, and appendix temperature experiments.

after.justification: v3 retains original attack experiments and adds sampling-schedule comparisons, REINFORCE-GCG results, and an analysis using 400 manually labelled completions.

M1.justification: Beyond renaming, v3 Section 5.1 adds uniform and trailing-block sampling schedules to v1's proposed optimize-then-sample approach. These change which intermediate prompts receive generation resources. The underlying attack optimizers and first-token entropy objective remain unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate harmful-response elicitation using the first 100 HarmBench prompts and the same four victim models. The new human-label audit examines existing response coverage; changes to attack methods and sampling schedules introduce no distinct dataset or task.

E2.justification: v3 adds REINFORCE-GCG to the reported attack comparisons and associated compute and optimization analyses; v1 only discusses its source work. Conversely, the direct-sampling versus Best-of-N results in v1 Appendix H disappear, although their implementation descriptions remain in v3 Appendix K.

E3.justification: The added schedule experiments compare query budgets and parameter-normalized FLOPs, including block size 5 and sampling budgets illustrated in Figures 4 and 32. Appendix J introduces a 400-completion audit with specified selection groups, and Appendix F adds an internal-judge substitution control. Existing base-attack hyperparameters are largely retained.

E4.justification: v3 adds comparisons testing schedule dependence, a human audit of judge false positives, and REINFORCE-GCG mechanism analyses, including a rerun with StrongREJECT as its internal judge. It removes v1 Appendix H's temperature-sensitivity experiments for direct sampling and Best-of-N. The entropy-response case studies are retained.

E5.justification: Appendix J adds classifier-precision estimation and a probabilistic correction of ASR using manual labels. The existing greedy-versus-sampling z-test, including p=0.063, is retained and moved to Appendix K. No repeated-run counts, seed reporting, or confidence intervals are added.

E6.justification: v3 reports new schedule, REINFORCE-GCG, and precision-adjusted results; Table 6 gives REINFORCE-GCG ASR@50 of 0.84 on Gemma 3 1B and 0.54 on Llama 2 7B DA. The retained GCG/Llama 3 CB ASR@50 entry changes from 0.11 to 0.12. Entropy-comparison values are unchanged after column reordering, while the temperature-result tables are removed.

T1.justification: v1's Definition 1 and Equations 1–4 formulate expected maximum harm over samples from a constrained prompt, with a K-replicate estimator and proxy optimization. v3 replaces this with maximum harm over an attack's collected generations and an Algorithm 1-based budget objective using individual optimization and sampling costs. This substantively changes the formal specification; neither version provides theorem proofs.

C1.justification: The central claims about sampling efficiency, overlooked harmful outputs, and the entropy objective persist. v3 emphasizes unified attack design and scheduling, and standardizes the headline improvement to 37 percentage points at equal FLOPs, replacing v1's inconsistent 35–48-point statements. The two-orders-of-magnitude efficiency claim remains.

C2.justification: v1 suggests refusal suppression is caused by the affirmative objective. v3 qualifies this explanation after observing similar behavior with REINFORCE-GCG and an internal-judge substitution, leaving the mechanism unresolved. It also credits PAIR with some optimization benefit, discusses false-positive bias, and updates the experimental limitation from two-stage approaches to static schedules.

D1.justification: v3 adds REINFORCE-GCG hyperparameters and internal-judge information, specifies PAIR's single stream, and states that reproduction code accompanies supplementary material. v1 instead provides a project-page link. v3 removes the sampling-sweep summary table and the explicit identification of the local Gemma-2-based StrongREJECT implementation; most other implementation details remain.

R1.justification: v3 adds Yang et al. (2025) as concurrent support for concerns about optimization effectiveness. Appendix B expands the existing attack taxonomy to distinguish optimization steps, optimization samples, and evaluation samples. The principal positioning against greedy evaluation and guided attack objectives remains, and Geisler et al. was already cited.

P1.justification: The title and terminology change from tail-aware to sampling-aware, accompanied by substantial abstract, introduction, and framework rewrites. Results are reorganized into separate efficiency, mechanism, and objective-design subsections. Appendix explanations and organization also change extensively, beyond the insertion of new scientific content.

P2.justification: v3 expands the introductory figure into a workflow diagram with performance bars and removes v1's introductory histogram display. The main ASR table moves to Appendix D and gains a bar-chart presentation. An algorithm box, schedule charts, and correction table are added; the compute heatmap axes change, and appendix plots are resized and extended.

improvement.justification: v3 makes the attack framework clearer, tests schedule dependence, and qualifies v1's mechanism explanation through additional controls. These strengthen the central argument. The net gain is limited by removal of temperature-sensitivity evidence and inconsistencies in the new human-validation analysis: Appendix J specifies a 59% baseline correction, but Tables 6–7 change 0.61 to 0.48 rather than approximately 0.36. Judge-error concerns therefore remain unresolved.
